{{Quote|Look into my face&mdash;it's the last thing you will ever see.|8t88, shortly before killing the majordomo|<ref name="Rebel Agent" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] served as a '''majordomo''' for the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] during his brief time as [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]]. The [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] remained at Jerec's [[Government House (Sulon)|Sulon headquarters]] after the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] had moved on, and continued to serve other masters. When the droid [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] [[8t88/Legends|8t88]] came to stay at the tower, the majordomo sent 8t88 to a coat room while passing it off as a VIP guest suite, as he thought that it was where an uppity droid belonged. However, 8t88 caught on to the majordomo's duplicity and&mdash;after reprimanding him&mdash;[[Death/Legends|killed]] the Human by breaking his neck. Afterwards, 8t88 noticed that the majordomo's death had invigorated the remaining staff.

==Biography==
===Imperial servant===
{{Quote|Summon the fool in charge.|8t88|<ref name="Rebel Agent" />}}
Sometime during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] served as a [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] for the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]],<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> an [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="The Dark Forces Saga Part 6">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050616a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 6: Outcasts and Megalomaniacs Welcome}}</ref> during Jerec's brief stint as [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]]<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> during the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="0 ABY Date">In the [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]], the majordomo mentions that [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] served as [[Governor/Legends|governor]] of [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]] five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of ''Rebel Agent''. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of ''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]'' to [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], which in turns gives Governor Jerec's rule a date of [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> The majordomo worked in the Sulon [[Government House (Sulon)|Government House]],<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> also referred to as the Dark Palace,<ref name="Strategy Guide">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> and after Jerec's departure, the majordomo continued to serve the executives who would go on to take residence in the house. Bragging about his work for the house's past masters eventually became a hobby of the decadent majordomo.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

===An uppity droid in its place===
{{Quote|Please! I'm sorry I gave offense&mdash;tell me how to make amends!"<br />"Ah, if only you could. But the malfunction is hidden within your skull. I don't know if you've seen any brains lately, but they're hard to sort out. A CPU makes more sense."<br />"My brain?"<br />"Why, yes. Assuming you have one.... You know, the organ that believes it's superior to machines, and enjoys making fun of them.|The majordomo and 8t88|<ref name="Rebel Agent" />}}
[[File:GovtHouse.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Dark Palace on Sulon]]
During the year [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]],<ref name="TNEC" /> the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] [[8t88/Legends|8t88]], who was under the employ of Jerec, took residence of the house while working on a project for the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]]. The majordomo was not fond of the droid,<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> and as such passed off a coat room as a luxurious VIP guest suite for 8t88 to stay in,<ref name="Audio Drama">[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]]</ref> hoping to impress the rest of the house's staff by doing so. When the droid noticed that his room was conjoined to the palace's ballroom, 8t88 realized that he had been fooled; miffed by the duplicity, 8t88 tasked his henchman [[Rol (Human)|Rol]] to find the majordomo. When the majordomo was informed of his summoning, he took his time in answering the call and made sure to precede Rol into 8t88's "guest suite" and entered it trying to hide his smile. 8t88 coyly asked what the history of the house was and asked the majordomo to start with the alleged suite.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> Initially, the majordomo began to explain the history of the entire structure itself before 8t88 instructed the man to focus solely on the room. Before the majordomo could answer, 8t88 pointed out how it was attached to the ballroom&mdash;an observation 8t88 noted as being odd&mdash;and requested to know for what the room was originally intended, specifically being interested in its "pedigree."<ref name="Audio Drama" />

The majordomo silently considered confessing to the droid, but figured that bluffing out of it would be less embarrassing. As such, he persisted that the coat room was a VIP suite, and that it was assigned to 8t88 because of the droid's rank and stature,<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> as well as the fact that it was the only room that could accommodate 8t88's pet [[hornagaunt]] [[Grendel]].<ref name="Audio Drama" /> When 8t88 asked for him to come closer, the majordomo assumed that his cover had worked. However, as soon as he within reach of the mechanical, 8t88 reached out and grabbed the majordomo's robes and pulled him so they were face to face and revealed that he had already seen through the man's lies. 8t88 wrapped his fingers around the majordomo's neck which caused him to [[urine/Legends|urinate]], as the man pleaded for mercy and promised to make amends. However, 8t88 rebuked him and crushed his facial bones with his robotic hand, along with screaming, fainting and finally [[Death/Legends|die]].<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> Afterwards, Grendel consumed the majordomo's body.<ref name="Audio Drama" />

The majordomo's fate made an example for the ramining staff, who served the droid more vigorously, and 8t88 was moved into a more luxurious study.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Greetings, your eminence. Can I be of service?.|The majordomo presents himself|<ref name="Rebel Agent" />}}
The Human majordomo was known to boast about his service to the Dark Palace's resident governors. The majordomo held himself in high esteem, taking his time in answering 8t88's call and preceding Rol into 8t88's chamber. Believing that he could impress the Palace staff<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> by putting 8t88 in a coat room,<ref name="Audio Drama" /> he became nervous when he believed that 8t88 had caught onto the deception and decided to bluff, thinking that would not be as embarrassing as confessing the truth. When addressing 8t88, the majordomo spoke with condescension in a manner that left Rol uneasy.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

When 8t88 made it clear that he was displeased with the majordomo's duplicity, the man urinated himself and begged for 8t88 to let the him make amends.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> However, 8t88 did not believe such a task was possible, claiming that the majordomo had a malfunction in his brain. In addition, 8t88 thought that the majordomo possessed a stigma against droids.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /><ref name="Audio Drama" />

The majordomo was light-skinned, and adorned himself with a flowing [[Color/Legends|red]] robe at the time of his death. The man was bald, but had black [[Hair/Legends|eyebrows]] and brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Did you send for the fool in charge of this place?|In the audio drama, 8t88 asks Rol if the latter had sent for the majordomo|<ref name="Audio Drama" />}}
The unnamed majordomo first appeared in the novella ''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]'', which was written by [[William C. Dietz]] and released during [[1998]]. The character appeared in one of the novella's illustrations, which was crated by artist [[Ezra Tucker]] (although the illustration with him is a few pages later than his actual appearance in the story).<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> The character later appeared in the novella's [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|full cast audio drama]], where his voice was provided by [[Bob Otto]].<ref name="Audio Drama" /> There are few differences in the scene between the novella and the audio drama. The most prominent difference is that the novella never clearly states where exactly the majordomo had placed 8t88; it only mentioned that 8t88's quarters were adjoined to a ballroom.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> The audio drama changes 8t88's dialogue in order to make it explicitly clear that the room was in fact a simple coatroom.<ref name="Audio Drama" /> Also in the novella, Rol goes to fetch the majordomo personally,<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> whereas in the audio drama Rol only sent for the majordomo, and did not retrieve him on foot. Finally, the audio drama added extra dialogue to make up for the lack of the readable prose that the novella offered.<ref name="Audio Drama" /> This article treats the novella as the correct depiction of events.
